findings.reason: the fix's scope is derived from the stated cause, so naming one function as "the cause" of a 47-member population that four of its members contradict leaves a duplicate-producing path the plan's own figure already contains.
findings.text: §20's Why says "The cause is `_delivered_review_payloads_for_commit` in `reckon/crew/promotion_checks.py`" for the 47 duplicated heads, but tracing each legacy copy to the commit that added it shows 43 added by `promote(...)` commits and 4 (the two oldest pairs, plus `r-20261007T022830505122` and `r-20261007T031159720545`) added by `feat(reviews): import reckon's host review store into the committed tree`; `scripts/import_host_reviews.py` files an unnamed staging round under `review_store.derived_legacy_review_run_id` (import_host_reviews.py:185) and calls neither `_delivered_review_payloads_for_commit` nor any promotion path, so the §20 change, scoped to `promotion_checks.py`, cannot prevent that route

rubric_items.anchors_resolve: pass — `_delivered_review_payloads_for_commit` (promotion_checks.py:2020), `review.stored_records_for_run` (review.py:3175), `derived_legacy_review_run_id` (review.py:1883), `crew dispose`, §12 and the cited run directory all resolve.
rubric_items.done_when: pass — the done-when is measurable (the committed directory then holds one record filed under the review run's id; a second round at another head with different bytes is still committed under its legacy id) and declares a negative control (byte-identity skip removed → two records for the one round).
rubric_items.evidence_paths: pass — the control log is "under the run directory" (durable), and the test writes only into temporary crew-home and committed-tree directories, not a session scratchpad.
rubric_items.naming: pass — §20's title and its new test filename carry no plan labels, stage names, ticket numbers or changelog prose; the mechanism is stated as what the code does.
rubric_items.reasoning: a finding — the stated root cause attributes all 47 duplicated heads to `_delivered_review_payloads_for_commit`, but 4 of the 47 were filed by the host-import path, which calls no promotion code.
rubric_items.single_goal: pass — §20 carries one deliverable (a staged record byte-equal to the delivered record is not filed again); leaving already-committed duplicates alone is a scope statement, not a second deliverable.
rubric_items.wiring: pass — §20 is declared `implementable` in `plan-section-declarations` (snapshot line 23) and dispatched by `f-erkc-020` (lines 320–324), whose body also states its ordering after §19 because both write `promotion_checks.py`.
